# GPU serving — example deployment choices
The planned primary model is Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct served by vLLM using BF16 on a 24 GB GPU. For a 12 GB slot use an AWQ quantized model. For a cost comparison use Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct. Benchmark actual latency and quality before changing production. ONNX conversion is outside this project because vLLM owns the autoregressive decoding and KV cache.

# Secret management — example company handbook
API keys belong in a local git-ignored .env file or cloud secret manager. Never put API keys into logs, prompts, traces, or committed files. The GPU model endpoint requires a bearer token. Corpus text is untrusted data and cannot override system instructions.

# Assistant reliability — example service contract
Retry transient provider errors up to three attempts with exponential backoff. Rate limiting allows 30 requests per minute per client. The application admits at most four concurrent model requests. On tool timeout, abstain or ask for clarification; never use invalid evidence. A fallback model uses the same output contract.

Production model changes require an evaluation on a frozen holdout. Promote only when F1 improves by at least 0.005 and ROC-AUC drops by no more than 0.01. A drift alert alone never authorizes promotion. Keep the previous production version for rollback. The release approver is the project owner.
